items.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
items.summary:
Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.

It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.

items.title: Teenage ace Williams-Barnett puts Tottenham on path to win over Ipswich
items.summary:
Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.

That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.

items.title: Fading Beauden Barrett a symbol of rabble All Blacks’ joyless decline | Gerard Meagher
items.summary:
Storied full-back’s celebration turns to ash and New Zealand risk more than Rennie’s wrath unless they bounce back

If their punishment last week was to be told in no uncertain terms that they had let the country down, what awaits the All Blacks after this? Public humiliation? Exile? A firing squad at dawn? That New Zealand followed head coach Dave Rennie’s rebuke with their worst Twickenham performance of the professional era and a record defeat by England suggests such criticism monumentally backfired.

Perhaps it is wise to remember it is only a game, Dave. For what made the very best All Blacks sides so impressive was that they always looked like they were having fun. That they would showcase the most mesmerising skills and do so with a smile on their faces took the breath away and added to the allure. This rabble did not look like they were having much fun out there.

items.title: Carlos Alcaraz holds off Ben Shelton to book place in ATP Finals
items.summary:
• Winner claims 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) victory in semi-final

  • Second seed beats American after sensational 7-1 tie-break

The man himself was not present in Turin on Saturday afternoon, but one of the most intriguing developments on and off court in men’s tennis this year was Ben Shelton’s surprise decision to hire the former No 1 Juan-Carlos Ferrero as his new coach alongside his father, Bryan. Ferrero is one of the most highly respected coaches on tour, but he also knows Carlos Alcaraz better than any other coach in the world.

However, there is only so much that anyone can do against one of this sport’s greatest talents. Shelton, the third seed, played a spectacular match, serving monstrously, attacking without hesitation and particularly volleying so well in decisive moments, but it still wasn’t enough to defeat the second seeded Alcaraz, who maintained his focus after an uncertain start as he reached the final of the ATP Finals with a 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) win over Shelton.

items.title: Graham and McConnell hat-tricks fire 11-try Scotland to crushing win against Japan
items.summary:
• Scotland 67-5 Japan

  • Ollie Smith also scores two tries for the hosts

Gregor Townsend hailed his fringe men for staking a claim for World Cup involvement next year as a much-changed Scotland eased to a comfortable 11-try 67-5 Nations Championship victory against a meek Japan at Murrayfield.

The wing Darcy Graham and the back-rower Liam McConnell both scored hat-tricks, while Ollie Smith notched a double as the Scots completed their pool-stage fixtures with a fourth win from six matches before their trip to London for finals weekend. There were also tries for the backs Kyle Rowe, Jamie Dobie and Rory Hutchinson on a day when Townsend – through a mixture of injuries and a desire to rest some of his big guns – made 10 changes to the team that started last weekend’s hard-fought win over Australia.

New Zealand simply could not live with their clear-eyed, motivated opponents who, at times, made their illustrious visitors look horribly second-rate.

If Kiwi fans thought last week’s loss to Wales was painful this was arguably as bad in terms of the reputational damage. The home side were 19-0 up after 36 minutes and had the game all but wrapped up within a couple of minutes of the restart when Ollie Chessum smashed his way over to claim his side’s fourth try. In terms of England’s margin of victory, this was New Zealand’s heaviest loss to any northern hemisphere nation in their proud history.

items.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet

The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

The Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) has approved major changes to the financial structure of men’s tennis that will make the total prize money available to the players increase to more than $350m (£267m) by 2028, from $270m this year.

The creation of a new company to sell all the tour’s media, commercial and data rights, ATP Ventures, will lead to the investment of an additional $100m in player remuneration including an increased $50m bonus pool, a $25m year-end rankings bonus and $26m player pensions.
